sections.title: Employment Contract
sections.text:
Ukusik walked out of the sealed-off Katorga district of Deity Grypherburg. She is trying her best not to look back, and to walk a path of her own.

If you'd like a little "bite," you can also call her Ukusik.

sections.title: Token
sections.text: A jet-black, glossy glass marble — who knows how it was fired. Heavy and perfectly round. Ukusik says it's her treasure, and you're not allowed to lose it to anyone.

sections.title: Profile
sections.text: Ukusik was formerly active in Deity Grypherburg, Ursus, as a member of the underground organization "Unfettered Alliance." She later joined Rhodes Island's Deity Grypherburg office on Operator Zima's recommendation, taking part in intelligence gathering and emergency first aid. At the request of her guardian, Leto, Ukusik reports to Rhodes Island headquarters at regular intervals to receive Oripathy treatment and a general education.

sections.title: Clinical Analysis
sections.text:
Imaging tests show the indistinct outlines of internal organs, obscured by abnormal shadows. Originium granules detected in the circulatory system. The subject is confirmed to be infected with Oripathy.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 8%
Distinct Originium crystal formations are visible across Operator Ukusik's limbs and torso, accompanied by old skin lesions. Medical imaging analysis further confirms a small amount of Originium crystal distribution in Operator Ukusik's upper respiratory tract.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.27u/L
Operator Ukusik spent long periods performing manual labor in a high-risk active Originium environment. Lacking both protective equipment and access to treatment, her Oripathy went unchecked in its early stages, resulting in impaired function across multiple organs. Fortunately, since arriving at Rhodes Island, Operator Ukusik has cooperated actively with her treatment and shown good compliance, and her physical condition has improved.

sections.title: Archive File 1
sections.text:
Her mother gave birth to her and died on a filthy sickbed; her father abandoned her and died in an alley where gamblers gathered.
At just three years old, she was "recruited" into a pipe-cleaning crew along with a group of other children. Carrying a rope and an iron brush taller than herself, she used her small, thin frame to crawl through the Originium-crusted energy conduits in the engine layer of Deity Grypherburg. She grew up inside those cramped, sweltering pipes. She got used to the darkness there, but never to the practiced silence of her companions. She saw far too many small creatures that had died trapped inside the pipes, and she collected the hard, round husks the insects left behind the way rich children collect jewels.
The gap-toothed old man they called "Captain" took the wages from their employer, but would only give the children a few slices of black bread to fill their stomachs; the rest of the money most likely went to drink — perfectly ordinary for an elderly male Ursus living in Deity Grypherburg. One day, the gap-toothed old man got drunk and forgot to lower the rope ladder and collect the children who had been waiting inside the pipes for hours.
She watched with her own eyes as her companions trampled one another for the last scraps of breathable air near the top, and in the end most of the children suffocated after inhaling too much toxic exhaust. She saw... the dead children's lips were rosy, a "healthy" flush had risen in their cheeks, and they even seemed to be wearing happy smiles.
She climbed to the highest point over the children's bodies, breathing the fresh air seeping in through the gap at the pipe's sealed hatch, and survived.
By the time the old man sobered up, remembered, and rushed to the site, she was already on the verge of losing consciousness. He was standing directly above her head, yet he refused to open the hatch until he had finished haggling over the price with the pipe supervisor.
To save on the cost of hauling away the bodies, the gap-toothed old man climbed down into the shaft himself to move the children's corpses. Having come to, she stood on the ground above, watching that reeking, liquor-soaked back with cold indifference...
She closed the hatch, sealing the old man in with the bodies, and then she left — What? How would I know where she went?
You thought this was about me? No, no, you've got it wrong. "She" is a friend of mine — her name is Sveta Goreva, and my name is Ukusik. Obviously not the same thing.
— Excerpt from "My Best Friend," an impromptu speech delivered by Operator Ukusik at the closing party of her writing course

sections.title: Archive File 2
sections.text:
When Operator Ukusik first arrived at Rhodes Island, the black fowlbeast that had followed her here caused a small commotion. Ukusik swears she released it outside Deity Grypherburg before setting out. Heaven only knows how it managed to keep up!
The fowlbeast has no name. Ukusik insists it is not her pet and that she has neither the duty nor the responsibility to feed it. As for whether it counts as some sort of rare animal, she has never studied the subject at all and so cannot answer.

[Catalogue Name]: Northern Sooty Rare Fowlbeast
[Distribution]: Sightings are concentrated in the far northern mining districts of Ursus and along the edges of the coniferous forests of southern Sami, with occasional appearances near the routes of certain nomadic cities.
[Rarity]: Extremely Rare
The Northern Sooty Rare Fowlbeast is a medium-sized resident fowlbeast; adults measure roughly 25-30 centimeters in length and are covered in dense, matte smoke-black plumage. Its beak is short and strong, and its eye-rings are usually yellow. Tiny fragments of Originium are often found clinging to the tips of its flight feathers. Whether this is a direct symptom of Oripathy infection or the result of a peculiar metabolism remains unclear.
The Northern Sooty Rare Fowlbeast is capable of mimicking ambient sounds, industrial noise in particular. The purpose behind this mimicry remains unclear; it may be nothing more than pure play.
Because this fowlbeast is exceedingly rare and highly wary, capturing a clear photograph of one has in recent years come to be regarded as a supremely challenging goal among fowlbeast photography enthusiasts.
— "Natural History of the Ursus Empire: Rare Creatures Volume (Fourth Edition)"

[Audio Log]
I'm recording this so nobody comes asking me how I picked it up again!
First off, I didn't pick it up at all — it decided that all on its own. It landed right on top of my head while I was bawling my eyes out over Matvey! My guess is it just wanted to stop for a bit of salt, and I happened to be crying a whole lot.
Second, I don't know its habits. I've never once seen it eat or drink anything, and it doesn't bother telling me where it's off to, either. My guess is it's nested somewhere near a factory boiler, because sometimes it flies over and it's hot to the touch, like a live coal!
Mimicking sounds? I don't really remember much. There was one time I dreamed I heard two people talking, and the talk kept getting deeper and deeper, and they said something like, "This land is nothing but a glass marble, laid out on a blanket of light-proof black velvet"... When I woke up, it was standing at my bedside staring at me with its little head tilted.
If you want a photo with it, go right ahead — just keep me out of the frame. And to those few big brothers and sisters who fainted, I'm very sorry. Better luck next time.

Even before Ukusik arrived at Rhodes Island headquarters, Operators who enjoy fowlbeast photography had spotted traces of a Northern Sooty Rare Fowlbeast nearby.
And so Rhodes Island's photography enthusiasts immediately applied to have their field rotations reshuffled, formed a special squad, and prepared to conquer this summit of fowlbeast photography in one go. After a week of trekking through the wilds, Operator Scene was the first to photograph a Northern Sooty Rare Fowlbeast. The composition and handling of light in that shot were not Scene's finest work, but it was more than enough to keep the photography squad celebrating the whole way home — right up until they walked back into Rhodes Island's living quarters and saw several dozen Operators crowded around Ukusik and the fowlbeast on her shoulder, snapping away with cameras of every kind, personal terminals, and even surveillance heads. Perhaps it was the long exhaustion combined with the sudden blow to their spirits, but several Operators in the photography squad fainted on the spot. Scene kept her serene expression; it was only when someone asked her to take a commemorative photo of them with that insufferably haughty Northern Sooty Rare Fowlbeast that she forgot she needed to take the lens cap off first.

The one on Ukusik's shoulder feels somehow different... It doesn't have a single speck of the Originium debris a Northern Sooty Rare Fowlbeast is supposed to have. Did you notice that too?
— An Operator from the photography squad

sections.title: Archive File 4
sections.text:
At the Doctor and Amiya's request, the Medical Department provided ample psychological counseling support to a number of those who lived through the "Katorga Incident," Ukusik among them. Ukusik, however, has consistently shown a high degree of resistance to the act of "telling." She habitually deflects with jokes, fake crying, and playing cute, and refuses to face the scenes of her inner trauma head-on — something we, as medical staff, are in no position to fault her for.
The turning point came on the second day after New Year. On her day off, Ukusik came to the counseling room of her own accord, picked the lock, sat down in the soft sofa, and said a great deal to the empty desk and chairs.
We cannot say whether her flipping the switch on the interview recorder was an accident, but in any case, the camera and microphone were working properly and faithfully recorded everything.

[Audio Log]
...I never told you about that house, did I?
I asked Yura and the others, and nobody knows how a poor kid like Matvey managed to build a house of his own. But on the day they were let out of prison, when a bunch of university students stripped of their student status and citizenship were standing around with no idea where to go, Matvey said to them, "Come with me." On the strength of that one simple line, he led those classmates in adding a second floor and a third onto the original house — he even built a little courtyard out front! That was the first base of those "Unfettered." They had plenty of other bases afterward, but in the very end, everyone still came back to that house...
Matvey said the legend went that the plot had originally been used to bury the dead, so it had stood empty all along. But when he dug the foundation, all he turned up was some Originium debris — nothing frightening at all.
Right, and the Originium too. Antosha noticed the stones on my body early on, but none of them said anything about it. I used to think black stones were the filthiest things there were, but after hearing them talk about the remarkable things the Infected had done, I started to feel that these black stones were actually the cleanest of all. Clean stones — nothing to be afraid of.
It was around this time in the year 110■ that I first found out Matvey had died in the sealed-off zone. A couple of days ago, I heard the latest news about Antosha from ■■, too. And I thought — if Matvey were still alive and knew what an amazing thing Antosha is doing now, what would he say? Maybe he'd say, "My friends are all walking the right road"?
I think it's a line from a song — I heard Matvey humming it once. He was sharpening a knife in the kitchen by the sunlight, and I was sitting at the table sorting the gold coins we'd stolen into stacks by denomination. In a little while Antosha would be back, and whether or not he'd been hurt, he always called out every single name in the house first. Matvey never answered — he'd only give a small nod. Honestly, it was such a wondrous feeling, and I didn't even know what to call it, because it was so unfamiliar to me!
God, just how long was I in that house?
Let me count — November, December... Was I really only with them for a mere forty-odd days?
No, how is that even possible?!
Only... forty-odd days?
But it really felt to me like it was—

sections.title: Promotion Record
sections.text:
"Hey, big sister, why do you keep staring at me?"
"You're hurt."
"You mean this? It's nothing! I just cut my finger on a blade. A scratch like this doesn't even register with me."
"It sounds like you've seen a few big things in your time."
"I've seen plenty of people die, you know... Didn't expect that, huh? Hehe!"
"When you're sad, you don't have to force yourself to smile."
"What a strange feeling... It's like there's something inside my head— Did you do that?"
"Don't be afraid, little one. I only smoothed over a few of your feelings. You should be able to feel something new now."
"My cheeks feel hot."
"And what else?"
"My nose is stinging."
"Is it because the smell of the New Year fireworks is too sharp?"
"No... It's because something bad happened during an earlier New Year. That's strange... I can't believe I'm telling you all this."
"It's not strange at all. After all, we're both Liberi from Ursus, and we just happen to be sharing the same bench at a New Year party."
"Being a Liberi in Ursus is so hard..."
"Finding a quiet corner at a Rhodes Island New Year party is hard too. Wherever you go, you can feel so very much joy and excitement."
"It sounds like those aren't things you'd need to run away from, though?"
"Then why are you here yourself?" The older Liberi gently stroked Ukusik's hair with her mechanical arm.
Ukusik pouted. "I guess I just don't dare let myself be happy."
"I see. I've heard that a person's heart is two rooms divided by a wall. Happiness lives in one of them, but it's always on edge, never daring to laugh too loudly, for fear of waking the pain that lives next door."
"Huh? I don't think that's what they said in general studies class. But go on..."
"But the truth is, when you feel happy, you have no idea what's actually living next door. Maybe the pain moved out long ago, and it's just an empty room."
"That makes sense. But how can I be sure?"
"That's when we need a key." The older Liberi held out a small badge, with a big smiling face on it, an antenna, and one word printed large.
"Courage." Ukusik read the word aloud.
"Courage is the key. Open the door to that other room and look inside — it's been empty for a long time now. No one will blame you, and no one will mind if you laugh too loudly. You could put all the words you wanted to say but never did in there, couldn't you?"
The older Liberi looked off into the distance. "Ah, my teammates are looking for me. I should go and join them."
"Wait, big sister! If I want to talk with you again later, how do I find you?"
"Don't worry, I'll find you first." The older Liberi laughed. "Besides, doesn't the badge I gave you have a communications antenna on it? You can whisper to it anytime you like."
Ukusik touched that "Courage" badge, and was suddenly seized by the urge to say something to the empty desk and chairs of the counseling room.
